title: Interactive Plotly Express
ques: Using `plotly.express`, write a snippet to create an interactive bar chart of 'sales' against 'month' from a DataFrame `df`.

answer.content:
import plotly.express as px

fig = px.bar(df, x='month', y='sales', title="Monthly Sales")
fig.show()

explanation: `plotly.express` (often imported as `px`) is a terse, consistent, high-level wrapper around the Plotly core library. It generates fully interactive web-based charts (with hover tooltips and zooming) using very little code.

title: Plotly Graph Objects

answer.content: While `plotly.express` is great for quick, standard charts, `plotly.graph_objects` provides lower-level, granular control over every aspect of the figure. You would use `go.Figure` when you need highly customized layouts, complex multi-trace charts (like overlaying a bar chart and a line chart on different axes), or customized subplots that Express cannot easily handle.

explanation: Graph Objects represent the underlying data structure of all Plotly charts.

title: Interactive Elements
ques: What are some of the built-in interactive features of Plotly charts rendered in a browser?

answer.content: By default, Plotly charts offer hover tooltips displaying exact data point values, zooming and panning, box-select and lasso-select tools, toggling traces on/off by clicking items in the legend, and an option to download the current view as a static PNG image.

explanation: These out-of-the-box interactive features make Plotly ideal for dashboards and web applications.
